advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Suppress the `_call_logged` WARNING for idempotent-success HTTP codes (404 on delete/get, 404/409 on link delete) so normal outcomes are not logged as failures.
evidence: `_call_logged` unconditionally logs on any Exception: transport.py:260-263 `except Exception as exc: logger.warning("jira-datacenter transport: %s failed for remote id %r: %r", member, remote_id, exc); raise`

`delete_issue` absorbs 404 as success AFTER `_call_logged` already logged it: transport.py:557-560 `_call_logged("delete_issue", ...)` then `except BackendHTTPError as exc: if exc.code == 404: return {"status": "already_absent", ...}`
`delete_issue_link` same pattern for 404/409: transport.py:580-586

`get_issue_by_rest`'s 404 is a NORMAL deletion signal consumed by `outbound_differ._safe_get_issue` (outbound_differ.py:137-139 maps `exc.code == 404` to `_DELETED`), yet transport.py:459 routes it through `_call_logged`, so every deleted-issue detection logs a spurious WARNING
advisory.finding: `_call_logged` logs a WARNING claiming failure for outcomes that are idempotent SUCCESS: a 404 in `delete_issue`, a 404/409 in `delete_issue_link`, and a 404 (deleted-issue detection) in `get_issue_by_rest`. These paths intentionally treat the HTTP error as the desired end-state, but the wrapper has already emitted `"<member> failed for remote id ... 404"` before the caller absorbs it, producing misleading noise in a story whose explicit goal is trustworthy observability.
advisory.suggested_fix: Perform the 404/409 idempotence check inside a variant that does not log those codes (e.g. pass an `ignore_codes` set to a non-logging call path), or make the delete/get methods catch the library error before `_call_logged` runs so idempotent outcomes never reach the WARNING branch.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Wire `isinstance(transport, TicketTransport)` (raising on failure) into `_build_jira_datacenter_backend` and the Cloud backend factory, per the ticket AC.
evidence: `_build_jira_datacenter_backend` builds and returns the backend with no conformance check: backend.py:185-188 `transport = JiraDataCenterTransport(...)` then `return JiraDataCenterBackend(transport=transport, client=client)`
No `isinstance(transport` occurs anywhere in the reconciler (search_files for `isinstance(transport` returned no matches; `TicketTransport` is not imported in either backend.py)

The changed docstring asserts the guard exists: _backend.py:200-204 '...so a construction-time conformance guard cannot be written against it at all' and _REQUIRED_TRANSPORT_MEMBERS comment '`isinstance(x, TicketTransport)` is defined against exactly this set'
Ticket bda8 AC: 'the conformance assertion runs where a backend is BUILT (`_build_jira_datacenter_backend` and the Cloud equivalent), so a missing member is a loud construction failure'
advisory.finding: The construction-time conformance guard that the new `@runtime_checkable` + `_TransportPortMeta.__instancecheck__` machinery exists to enable is never wired into the backend factories. `_build_jira_datacenter_backend` (and the Cloud factory) construct the transport without any `isinstance(transport, TicketTransport)` assertion, so a transport missing a required member still fails at a call site, not at construction — the outcome the metaclass docstring and the ticket AC say this change prevents.
advisory.suggested_fix: In each backend factory, after constructing the transport, add `if not isinstance(transport, TicketTransport): raise TypeError(...naming missing members...)` before returning the backend.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Bound `get_parent_map`'s offset loop (e.g. break when a page does not advance the max seen offset, or cap total pages) so a server ignoring `startAt` cannot loop forever.
evidence: Loop terminates only on empty page: transport.py:532-534 `if not batch: break` then `start_at += len(batch)`

Cloud's counterpart terminates on an explicit cursor signal, not emptiness: acli_graph.py:197-198 'The loop terminates when the response reports `isLast: true` or yields a null/absent `nextPageToken`'
The held-out test covers server-side maxResults truncation (test_transport_port_completeness_heldout.py:243-250) but not a server that ignores `startAt`, so the infinite-loop edge is untested
advisory.finding: `get_parent_map` paginates by advancing `start_at += len(batch)` and terminates only on an empty page. A DC server that ignores or clamps `startAt` (returning the same non-empty page repeatedly) never yields an empty batch, producing an infinite loop. Unlike Cloud's `nextPageToken`/`isLast` cursor, there is no total/page-count bound as a safety net.
advisory.suggested_fix: Track the previous `start_at`; if a full-looking page does not increase the set of new keys or `len(batch) == 0`, or after a sane max-page cap, break. Alternatively break when `len(batch) < page_size` AND the server is known to honor startAt, else guard with a page-count ceiling.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Document/handle the epic-parent NotImplementedError so it does not produce perpetual per-pass re-emission churn (e.g. suppress the parent op for known-unsupported epic parents rather than retrying it every pass), pending the greenhopper spike.
evidence: DC declines epic parents: transport.py:687-702 `if not is_subtask: ... raise NotImplementedError(...)`
Caller swallows it (not just HTTPError): dispatch_one.py:565-571 `except Exception as exc: ... logger.warning(...)`

The churn pathology this recreates is documented at the same call site: dispatch_one.py:525-529 '...the differ re-emitted the identical parent mutation on every pass — the perpetual `fields=['parent']` re-emission (~230 steady-state mutations...)'
advisory.finding: `set_parent` raises `NotImplementedError` for any non-subtask (epic) parent. The sole caller `dispatch_one._update_one_apply_parent` swallows it via a broad `except Exception`, so it will not crash — but because the parent is never applied, the next inbound snapshot shows no parent and the differ re-emits the parent mutation on every pass. This reproduces the perpetual re-emission churn the same function documents for the pre-8b25 parent bug, for every epic-typed parent on DC.
advisory.suggested_fix: Until the greenhopper Epic-Link path lands, have the caller (or a binding marker) record the epic-parent as intentionally-unsupported so the differ stops re-emitting it, rather than re-attempting and re-declining on every pass.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm `_identity_of`'s `accountId or name` fallthrough is intended for the assignee path and for empty-string accountId, and note it in the docstring (or gate the fallback on `accountId` being absent rather than falsy).
evidence: `account_id`: `raw.get("accountId") or raw.get("name")` — inbound_fields.py:178
`_identity_of` is used for both fields: inbound_fields.py:225 `out["assignee_identity"] = _identity_of(...)` and :227 `out["reporter_identity"] = _identity_of(...)`
Docstring justifies the precedence only for the reporter/Cloud-vs-DC case (:160-172) and does not mention the assignee path or the empty-string-accountId fallthrough
advisory.finding: `_identity_of` now returns `raw.get("accountId") or raw.get("name")` and is applied to BOTH assignee_identity and reporter_identity. The `or` treats a present-but-empty-string `accountId` as absent and falls through to `name`, and the change silently affects the assignee path too, not only the reporter path the ticket analyzed.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make `test_validate_assignee_exists_returns_the_dc_username` actually construct a DC transport with a fake client, call `validate_assignee_exists`, and assert the returned DC username (and that AssigneeNotFoundError is raised on a definitive miss / that matching is exact, not substring).
evidence: def test_validate_assignee_exists_returns_the_dc_username(monkeypatch) -> None:
docstring: "Cloud returns an accountId; DC has none, so DC must return the USERNAME. Returning `True`, or an accountId-shaped value, corrupts the identity."
body is only: `cls = _dc_transport_class()` then `assert hasattr(cls, "validate_assignee_exists")`
transport.py:741-744 implements exact-match (name/emailAddress/displayName) returning `str(_user_attr(user, "name") or assignee)` and raising AssigneeNotFoundError on miss — none of which is asserted
advisory.finding: `test_validate_assignee_exists_returns_the_dc_username` asserts only `hasattr(cls, 'validate_assignee_exists')` while its docstring names a precise return-value contract (DC must return the USERNAME, never `True` or an accountId-shaped value, because the caller flows the return on as the resolved identity). It never invokes the method or inspects a return value, so it cannot detect a regression in the behavior it claims to guard — an existence-only check mislabeled as a behavioral one.
advisory.suggested_fix: Instantiate `JiraDataCenterTransport.__new__(...)` with a fake `_client.search_users` returning a User whose `name` matches; assert the return equals the username. Add a negative case where search returns a substring-only hit and assert `AssigneeNotFoundError` is raised (exact-match contract), and a case where both name and accountId-shaped fields exist, asserting `name` is returned.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a DC-transport test that calls `set_entity_property`/`set_issue_property` against a fake client and asserts `add_issue_property` was invoked with the value passed VERBATIM (not wrapped as `{"value": ...}`), with the exact key.
evidence: transport.py:621-625 forwards `lambda: self._client.add_issue_property(remote_id, property_key, value)`
docstring bug 0b27: "an earlier Cloud implementation wrapped it as `{\"value\": …}` — which stored the wrong shape and broke correlation WITHOUT ever raising"
search `add_issue_property` across tests/unit/rebar_reconciler: no matches
new held-out file asserts only `hasattr(TicketTransport, 'set_entity_property')` / `hasattr(_dc_transport_class(), member)`
advisory.finding: The property-write verbatim-value contract (`_put_property`/`set_issue_property`/`set_entity_property`) is untested. The docstring explicitly calls out that an earlier Cloud implementation wrapped the value as `{"value": …}`, storing the wrong shape and breaking correlation WITHOUT ever raising (bug 0b27), yet no test asserts the value reaches `add_issue_property` verbatim.
advisory.suggested_fix: Inject a fake client that records `add_issue_property(remote_id, key, value)` args; assert the recorded value is identically the passed object/dict, not `{"value": value}`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a DC-transport test asserting `set_reporter` calls `issue.update(fields={"reporter": {"name": <username>}})` (DC payload shape), not Cloud's accountId shape.
evidence: transport.py:654-658 `lambda: issue.update(fields={"reporter": {"name": account_id}})`
search `set_reporter` in tests: hits are in test_identity_264f_* / test_transport_exception_contract_heldout, all against the ACLI/Cloud client, plus the presence-only entry in the new file
new held-out file only checks `hasattr` for `set_reporter`
advisory.finding: `set_reporter`'s DC-specific payload shape `{"reporter": {"name": account_id}}` is untested for the DC transport. The docstring stresses DC uses `name` rather than Cloud's `accountId`; a regression emitting `{"accountId": ...}` or the wrong nesting would not be caught (existing `set_reporter` tests in the suite target the ACLI/Cloud client, not the DC transport).

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add DC-transport tests for `delete_issue`: 404 returns already_absent, 403 raises PermissionError, other codes propagate.
evidence: transport.py:556-566 branches on `exc.code == 404` / `== 403` / else re-raise
new held-out file's `_REQUIRED` includes `delete_issue` but only via `hasattr` presence test
no test constructs a DC transport whose delete raises BackendHTTPError
advisory.finding: `delete_issue` error mapping (404 → `{status: already_absent}`, 403 → `PermissionError`, other codes re-raise) is untested. These are idempotence/rollback contracts the docstring says callers special-case, but no test drives a fake raising `BackendHTTPError(404)`/`(403)`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a DC-transport test asserting `delete_issue_link` returns already_absent when the client raises BackendHTTPError(404) and BackendHTTPError(409), and re-raises other codes.
evidence: transport.py:584-587 absorbs `exc.code in (404, 409)`
docstring: "a raced 404 would escape and unwind the pass ... Owning idempotence here makes the DC path correct"
search `delete_issue_link` in tests: DC transport is not exercised for its 404/409 absorption; hits are the ACLI/Cloud path and the presence-only entries in the new file
advisory.finding: `delete_issue_link` idempotence absorption (404/409 → already_absent inside the transport) is untested for the DC transport. The docstring makes this the central reason the transport owns absorption (the core handler only catches the Cloud-specific `subprocess.CalledProcessError`), so its absence is a real gap.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add DC-transport tests for `set_parent`: a sub-task issuetype writes `{"parent": {"key": ...}}` (and `{"parent": None}` for clear); a non-subtask raises NotImplementedError.
evidence: transport.py:687-704: `if not is_subtask: raise NotImplementedError(...)` else `issue.update(fields=body)`
search `NotImplementedError` in tests/unit/rebar_reconciler: no hits against the DC transport set_parent
new held-out file only asserts `hasattr` / value-form audit for `set_parent`
advisory.finding: `set_parent`'s branch contract is untested: writing `fields.parent` for a sub-task vs. raising `NotImplementedError` for a non-subtask (epic reparenting decline). This is a behavior the story exists to enforce (loud decline over silent no-op), but no test drives both issuetype branches.
